features.feature_value: Used a two-step check: look for personal insults/uncivil language first, then evaluate whether the ideas advance the debate.
features.evidence_span: whether there were personal insults that lack respectful debate... whether the ideas moved the debate forward.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes criteria about insults and whether ideas move the discussion forward.

features.feature_value: Tried to be fair to both sides while preventing content from becoming too derogatory toward a group.
features.evidence_span: Trying to see what was fair for both sides... allow it to be too derogatory towards a particular crowd.
features.rationale: They describe allowing balance but removing when derogation crosses a threshold.

features.feature_value: Believes in freedom of speech broadly, but draws the line at unwanted/unwarranted profanity and rejected only on that basis.
features.evidence_span: I believe society has freedom of speech... I draw the line when citizens are subjected to unwanted and unwarranted profanity. I only rejected responses when profanity was used.
features.rationale: They state a clear rule for rejection tied specifically to profanity.

features.feature_value: Generally open to free speech, but would not allow posts advocating violence or using curse words.
features.evidence_span: open to free speech... allow any posts that adcvocated violence or used curse words.
features.rationale: They provide explicit exclusion criteria for violence advocacy and curse words.

features.feature_value: Would remove aggressive/instigative content even if one post in the pair seemed acceptable; removing both helps filter problematic material.
features.evidence_span: Even if one of the pair was passable, it was worth removing both of them in order to filter out the problematic posts.
features.rationale: They describe a pair-level strategy: if one is problematic, remove both.

features.feature_value: Could not justify removing either; ended up keeping both posts in almost all cases.
features.evidence_span: I could not see getting rid of both posts, so I just kept both, in almost all cases.
features.rationale: They indicate an inability to separate judgments within the pair and a default to keeping both.

features.feature_value: Judged by whether posts made more sense vs sounded angry; both sometimes seemed angry.
features.evidence_span: Some post made more sense to me, while others just sounded angry.
features.rationale: They reference a content-cue contrast (sense vs anger) as their basis.

features.feature_value: Read both and based the decision on how much they agreed with each; agreement led to keeping both.
features.evidence_span: I saw how much I agreed with each. If I agreed with each then I felt like both could be posted.
features.rationale: They explicitly describe agreement as the decision rule for keep/remove.
